memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Sokoh, Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (that is, Debir), Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon and Giloh—eleven towns and their villages; Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron) and Zior—nine towns and their villages - Josh 15:48-54 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The inheritance climbs now into the hill country, listing towns among the heights — including Hebron, the very place given to faithful Caleb. This was higher, harder ground than the lowlands, yet it too was carefully counted as part of God's gift. The high places and the low places alike belonged to Judah's inheritance.

There is quiet encouragement in that. Not all of the inheritance was easy, gentle terrain. Some of it was hill country — steep, demanding, requiring effort to hold and cultivate. Yet the difficult heights were just as much God's gift as the fertile valleys. God's blessings are not always found on comfortable ground. Sometimes the richest portions of our inheritance lie in the harder, higher places of life.

This is worth remembering when God leads us into difficult terrain. The hard seasons, the uphill stretches, are not signs that we have left the inheritance behind — they may be part of it. Caleb found his reward in the hill country, not the easy lowland. And Jesus Himself walked the hardest ground of all, the road to the cross, and there won the greatest inheritance for us (Heb 12:2). Do not despise the high, hard places God assigns. They are often where the deepest blessings are found.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you in "hill country" — a difficult, uphill season right now?
- Can you trust that hard terrain may still be part of God's good gift to you?
- How does Christ walking the hardest road for you encourage you in yours?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me not to despise the hard, high places You lead me through. Teach me to trust that even the difficult terrain is part of the inheritance You have given in Christ. Amen.
